title: AquaPredict Milestone 7 Drainage-Informed Route Planner Metadata
disclaimer: RESEARCH & DEMONSTRATION PROTOTYPE — NOT A CERTIFIED NAVIGATION OR EMERGENCY EVACUATION SYSTEM

study_area.name: Downtown Houston / Buffalo Bayou Pilot Sector

cost_formulation.equation: Cost(e) = C_base * (1 + w_susc * EWSI) + P_depth + P_drain + P_uncert
cost_formulation.non_negative_guarantee: Cost(e) >= C_base > 0 for all edges under all scenarios and parameter values

base_travel_cost.definition: Geometric segment length in survey meters (derived from Shape.STLength)

terrain_susceptibility_factor.definition: 1.0 + (w_susc * EWSI_mean), where EWSI is the length-weighted continuous Exploratory Waterlogging Susceptibility Index [0.0 - 1.0]

modelled_depth_penalty.definition: Piecewise non-linear penalty based on maximum modelled ponding depth d_max from M5 simulation at selected preset and timestep

drainage_screening_penalty.definition: Screening penalty for proximity (< 25m street corridor) to M6 stormwater conduits with capacity exceeded (Qinflow > Qcap) or high loading

data_uncertainty_penalty.definition: Penalty applied when hydraulic information is missing or segment extends outside the 0.97 km² pilot grid. Missing data is never treated as evidence of safety.

speed_and_travel_time_assumptions.pedestrian_walking_speed_source: AASHTO / MUTCD default pedestrian walking speed standard (4.8 km/h, 3.0 mph)
speed_and_travel_time_assumptions.vehicular_speed_source: Municipal City of Houston SPEED attribute when present, defaulting to 30.0 mph for local streets

shortest.name: Shortest Route
shortest.reporting: Calculates and reports waterlogging exposure along the shortest route for comparison.

lowest_exposure.name: Lowest Waterlogging Exposure
lowest_exposure.objective: Prefers routes with lowest estimated water depth and exposure, penalizes waterlogging, avoids segments exceeding mode thresholds when alternatives exist
lowest_exposure.cost_metric: 2-pass algorithm: Pass 1 strictly excludes impassable segments (hard exclusion); Pass 2 falls back to lexicographic minimal-impassable routing if no 100% passable path exists in network. Base length + non-linear depth penalty + affected length penalty + uncertainty penalty.
lowest_exposure.reporting: Recommends detour when shortest route encounters hazardous or impassable water.

drainage_informed.name: Drainage-Informed Route
drainage_informed.objective: Integrates M1 terrain susceptibility (EWSI), M5 flood depth, and M6 subsurface storm conduit capacity screening
drainage_informed.reporting: Screened against subsurface drainage loading while clearly distinguishing conduit capacity from surface ponding.

pedestrian.description: Experimental screening thresholds for pedestrian footing stability (~10cm ankle depth caution, ~25cm shin depth impassable). Uncalibrated prototype assumption.

vehicle.description: Experimental screening thresholds for passenger sedans (~15cm exhaust splash caution, ~30cm air intake stall / float impassable). Uncalibrated prototype assumption.

measured_administrative_records: City of Houston Enterprise GIS street centerlines geometry and segment lengths
Street name, road classification, and municipal speed limits (defaulting to 30mph when null)
Storm sewer conduit diameters, materials, lengths, and spatial alignments
uncalibrated_model_estimates: M1 Exploratory Waterlogging Susceptibility Index (EWSI) derived from 1m LiDAR DEM topographic slope

M5 water depths derived from conceptual aggregate depression-filling drawdown model (uniform proportional filling of DEM sinks, 5% aggregate linear reservoir drawdown, SCS CN=88 runoff; unvalidated against high-water marks and NOT a 2D hydrodynamic Saint-Venant solver)
M6 stormwater conduit gravity capacities calculated via Manning's equation (n=0.013 assumed; conduit slope estimated from invert elevations when available, otherwise flagged incalculable)
M6 dynamic conduit surcharge ratios Q/Qcap based on contributing inlet fraction and lumped scenario inflow
assumed_screening_defaults: Pedestrian walking speed: 1.34 m/s (AASHTO / MUTCD standard)
Pedestrian caution threshold: 0.10 m (4 inches, ankle-depth wading nuisance; assumed screening threshold)
Pedestrian impassable threshold: 0.25 m (10 inches, shin-depth stability loss risk; assumed screening threshold)
Vehicle default speed: 30.0 mph (urban local street default)
Vehicle caution threshold: 0.15 m (6 inches, exhaust/splash risk; assumed screening threshold from NOAA/NWS 'Turn Around Don't Drown')
Vehicle impassable threshold: 0.30 m (12 inches, passenger sedan air intake stall/float limit; assumed screening threshold)
scientific_data_classification.temporal_nature: STATIC_SCENARIO_SNAPSHOT: Routing is evaluated as a static snapshot at a single chosen rainfall scenario timestep (default: Minute 60 storm peak). It is NOT dynamic time-dependent or time-expanded trajectory routing.

scientific_guardrails: Prototype Disclaimer: This route planner is an experimental research and demonstration prototype, NOT a certified navigation system or emergency evacuation service.
Relative Prototype Metric: The calculated hazard score is a relative multi-criteria screening metric, not a calibrated probability of flooding, property damage, or injury.
No Automatic Road Closure: Drainage capacity flags from M6 indicate subterranean hydraulic surcharge screening and must NOT be used to automatically declare streets closed.
Uncalibrated Model Outputs: M5 depth inputs are provisional simulation estimates from an uncalibrated 5% aggregate drawdown model and have not been validated against high-water marks.
Missing Data Governance: Missing terrain, depth, or drainage attributes are penalized as uncertain; missing data is NEVER treated as proof that a route is safe.
Strict Pilot Scope: Confined to the 0.97 km² Downtown Houston study domain. Extrapolation outside this boundary is unverified.
